newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip on lower spot prices.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip on lower spot prices.

text.p: Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly lower in subdued trade on Thursday, weighed down by weaker spot prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from four to eight yen per gram lower, with benchmark October ending down eight at 1,340 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from four to 12 yen per gram down. Benchmark October was lower by 12 yen at 1,359 yen.
In the gold bullion market, constant long-liquidation by overseas speculators pushed down bullion prices.
Spot gold was lower at $372.40/70 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $373.10/60 in New York on Wednesday.
In gold futures, Japanese private investors were generally sidelined as the market received little support from the currency market ahead of the U.S. holidays.

Traders said spot gold was still vulnerable to downside risk and they expected it to probe downside support at $370 per ounce. The market was watching to see if gold lease rates would rise from the current 2.5 percent over the next month, a trader said.
Platinum futures were pressured by private investors' long-liquidation, while Japanese traders sold spot platinum in arbitrage.

Traders said the Japanese platinum futures market was bearish on technicals, as the market could be pressured later this year by massive long positions still held by investors in the December contract. "Investors were unable to liquidate their longs as the market has been on a downward trend. The large positions still undermine sentiment," one trader said. Benchmark October silver contract was down by 0.6 yen per 10 grams at 176.1 yen.
Benchmark October palladium was down two yen per gram at 420 yen.
